bugs.title: An 'is empty' / 'is not empty' rule crashes the vendor's onboarding form
bugs.steps:
1. Template with a rule 'Country IS EMPTY → hide State' (or 'GSTIN IS NOT EMPTY → require certificate').
2. Start onboarding for a prospect with it.
3. Vendor opens the form and types anything into Country (or GSTIN).
bugs.expected: State appears (or the certificate becomes required); the form keeps working. On load, State is hidden while Country is empty.
bugs.actual: The whole page is replaced by 'Oops! Something Broke Down…' with 'TypeError: e is not a function' in the console. The vendor cannot fill that field at all. On load the rule also never applies: State is shown while Country is empty. The Studio offers and saves both comparisons, and the backend evaluates them; the form's comparison list has no entry for them.

bugs.title: Rules never undo when the vendor changes the answer back
bugs.steps:
1. Template T3: Foreign hides GSTIN; MSME shows and requires Udyam; not Indian requires turnover.
2. Vendor picks Foreign, then MSME, then Indian.
bugs.expected: Indian: GSTIN visible again, Udyam hidden, turnover optional (the form returns to the template's default).
bugs.actual: GSTIN stays hidden, so an Indian vendor can never enter the GSTIN the template requires, and Submit goes through without it. Udyam stays visible and required, turnover stays required. Same for numbers: employees 150 → 20 keeps HR policy required; turnover 25 lakh → 9 lakh keeps SWIFT shown. Only a draft Reset restores the form.

bugs.title: An AND rule fires when only one of its conditions is true
bugs.steps:
1. Template rule: Vendor type IS Foreign AND Annual turnover > 10,00,000 → show and require SWIFT code.
2. Fresh form: choose Foreign with turnover empty. Separately: choose Indian and type 25,00,000.
bugs.expected: SWIFT stays hidden in both cases; it appears only for Foreign with turnover above 10 lakh.
bugs.actual: SWIFT code appears with * in both cases. The form checks only the answer just changed, so an AND rule behaves like OR. Vendors are asked for fields that do not apply to them.

bugs.title: 'Contains' on a text answer works as 'is exactly' on the vendor form
bugs.steps:
1. Template rule: Company name CONTAINS 'Pvt' → require CIN.
2. Vendor types 'QA Steel Pvt Ltd'. Then types exactly 'Pvt'.
bugs.expected: 'QA Steel Pvt Ltd' makes CIN required (the Studio preview does this).
bugs.actual: 'QA Steel Pvt Ltd' leaves CIN optional. Only the exact text 'Pvt' makes CIN required. The Studio preview and the live form disagree.

bugs.title: A number rule compares as text when its limit is saved as text
bugs.steps:
1. Template rule: Number of employees IS GREATER THAN '100' (limit saved as text).
2. Fresh form: type 50, then 99.
bugs.expected: 50 and 99 are not more than 100, so HR policy stays optional (the backend compares these as numbers).
bugs.actual: HR policy becomes required for 50 and 99 (text order: '5' > '1'). With the limit saved as the number 100 the same rule works. Which form the Studio saves was not confirmed here, so this matters if any template carries text limits.

bugs.title: Attachment limited to PDF accepts a Word file
bugs.steps:
1. Template T1: Company brochure, attachment, allowed type PDF.
2. Vendor uploads brochure.docx and submits.
bugs.expected: The .docx is refused with a message that only PDF is allowed.
bugs.actual: The upload dialog accepts brochure.docx, the field shows it, and the response is submitted with it. The buyer sees 'brochure.d…' in the vendor's answers.

obs: Rule behaviour on the vendor form was checked twice: by the runner, and by probes that reset the draft and reload before every step, so stickiness could not mask a comparison.

The saved draft is restored about 7 seconds after the form appears. Anything typed before that is overwritten. Earlier validation runs (T2, T2B, T2C) were affected and are left out; T2D is the clean run.
The format mask on PAN does not force capitals; lower-case 'abcde1234f' is kept as typed (and then refused by the format check).
The buyer form is copied for each vendor the first time Send For Approval is opened; later changes to the buyer-form template do not reach that vendor.
A date set with the calendar's Today button showed on screen but was not saved once (T5); picking a day saved it. Today worked in T1, so this is noted, not filed.
Mapped answers (entity mappings, e.g. supplier code) are written to the vendor record only when the onboarding is accepted, not on submit.

A required buyer-form dropdown with no options blocks Send For Approval with only 'Please fill …'. This happened with the QA buyer form's payment-terms source, which has no data on PROCOL DEMO; it was switched to the currency list.
Creating a buyer-form template makes it the company's active buyer form: the backend picks the newest one. Creating one in the Studio silently replaces the existing form for every new approval.

tpl.T1: All field types — 2 sections: text (required, helper), long text, number, date, dropdown, multi-select, radio, PDF attachment, email, read-only, hidden
tpl.T2: Validations — PAN (format + PAN check), GSTIN must contain PAN, account number + re-enter (must match, no paste), IFSC format, mobile format
tpl.T3: Conditional logic — Foreign hides GSTIN; MSME shows + requires Udyam; not Indian requires turnover; company name contains 'Pvt' requires CIN; ISO 9001 requires certificate; Country empty hides State
tpl.T4: Prefill and data sources — legal name / email / address from the vendor's Procol profile; currency, country, region lists; Country resets Region; supplier code written back to the vendor record
tpl.T5: Three sections, every field required — text, number, dropdown, date, long text, attachment
tpl.T6: Empty, number and AND rules (limits saved as text) — Foreign AND turnover > 10 lakh shows SWIFT; employees > 100 requires HR policy; GSTIN not empty requires certificate
tpl.T7: Same as T6 with the limits saved as numbers
